recommendedTeachingNotes.note: 会う means to meet or see a person, including someone already familiar. Portuguese conhecer and German kennenlernen specifically emphasize first acquaintance.
暖かい is pleasantly warm weather/air. 暑い is hot weather; 熱い is an object/liquid hot to the touch.
お腹 names the belly/abdomen. 胃 is the internal stomach organ; casual stomachache expressions may use a broader body-region idiom.
Japan counts the ground/entrance level as 1階, so 4階 is the fourth level, equivalent to the third floor above the ground floor in ground-floor-plus-number systems.
A kōban is a small staffed Japanese neighborhood police station/post; it is not merely a telephone booth.
生徒 commonly refers to a school pupil or a learner under a teacher. German Schüler differs from university Student; French élève differs from higher-education étudiant.
どんな modifies a following noun: what kind of book? Standalone what uses a different grammatical construction in several languages.

杯 counts filled cups/glasses/bowls; the physical container comes from context. The existing Western glass forms are acceptable and do not require changing the English cup form solely for this counter.
半 means half. 二時半 is 2:30; German calls 2:30 halb drei, literally half [to] three. Keep this example outside the assessed answer/audio string.
必ず means without fail/definitely. In an instruction it can imply be sure to or must; it is not normally a polite reply meaning of course.
複雑 is commonly a na-adjective: 複雑な問題, a complicated problem. 複雑さ expresses the abstract noun complexity.

適当 can mean appropriate/suitable, but in a different context it can mean casual, careless, or perfunctory. The assessed isolated card selects the suitable sense; the careless sense needs its own example.
熱心 commonly describes someone enthusiastic, eager or diligent about an activity: 熱心な学生, an eager/diligent student. 熱心に勉強する means to study earnestly.
Practice a sport here means train/rehearse skills, not only play that sport regularly.

remainingLimitations.issue: Grammatical gender, articles and inflection are not fully taught by isolated forms.
remainingLimitations.evidence: The snapshot supplies one string per language, with many default masculine adjective/person forms and articleless nouns.
remainingLimitations.implication: A correct isolated translation does not by itself teach the appropriate feminine/plural form, agreement, or noun gender.
remainingLimitations.suggestedAction: Add contextual examples and language-specific article/gender/inflection metadata; avoid treating unprovided gender variants as inherently wrong.

remainingLimitations.issue: Politeness/register and regional variants need explicit learner context.
remainingLimitations.evidence: Standalone grammar and sentence rows mix tú/usted and tu/vous, and the Portuguese material is mainly Brazilian while some neutral/European vocabulary remains. English you alone cannot specify these choices.
remainingLimitations.implication: Most reviewed choices are valid, but a single universal one-to-one translation cannot express all social and regional distinctions.
remainingLimitations.suggestedAction: Label selected register/dialect and show alternatives in notes; do not mechanically force every valid sentence into one register.

remainingLimitations.issue: Dictionary senses require contextual teaching beyond the corrected display strings.
remainingLimitations.evidence: Examples include 適当 suitable versus careless, 上手/下手 skill at an activity, Japanese family honorifics, and counting filled containers.
remainingLimitations.implication: The complete text review improves trustworthiness but cannot guarantee conversational teaching quality from a vocabulary string alone.
remainingLimitations.suggestedAction: Use the concrete notes above and maintain sentence-level explanations; seek speaker review and learner feedback where available without purchasing services.
